disease_hierarchy_method: Eligible child evidence belongs to the selected general category. Parent-direct estimates are preferred within each overlapping study/population; otherwise one adjusted/primary child estimate is selected. Disjoint populations require explicit documentation.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 1.07 (95% CI: 0.51–2.23), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin B1 and kidney and renal pelvis cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 85.51%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
